chunks: And 'Ulan narrated, he said: Dharif Abu Nasr the servant narrated to me

He said: I entered upon him -meaning the Master of the Age (peace be upon him)- and he said to me: Bring me the red sandalwood. (He said): I brought it to him, and he (peace be upon him) said: Do you know me? I said: Yes. He said: Who am I? I said: You are my master, and the son of my master. He said: I did not ask you about this. Dharif said: I said: May Allah make me your ransom, explain to me. He said: I am the seal of the successors, and through me Allah wards off calamity from my family and my Shia.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الزَّمَانِ: Master of the Age (referring to Imam al-Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the title 'Seal of the Successors' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Dharif Abu Nasr recounts a profound dialogue with Imam al-Mahdi (peace be upon him), who corrects the servant’s general identification to emphasize his unique theological rank as the 'Seal of the Successors' (Khatam al-Awsiya'). This title underscores his role as the final in the line of Imams who inherit the Prophet’s spiritual authority, serving as the divine instrument through whom God shields the faithful from calamity.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 215 - It is narrated from Allaan Razi from the servant, Dharif Abu Nasr: “I came to the Master of the time (a.s) and he told me to bring red sandalwood, which I did. Then he asked: Do you know me? I said: Yes. He asked: Who am I? I said: My master, and the son of my master. He said: I did not ask you this. Tareef said: I said: May I be sacrificed on you, tell me. He said: I am the seal of the successors; and through me will Allah, the Mighty and Sublime ward off calamities from my family and my Shia.”
